questions.title: Define system software
questions.text: Define the term **system software**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Software that manages / controls / maintains the computer (hardware) (1)
- and provides a platform for other software / applications to run (1)

Accept a correct example in place of the second point only if a description is also given.

points.criterion: Manages / controls / maintains the computer or hardware
Provides a platform for applications / runs in the background / not for a user's task

scheme.model_answer: Programs that manage and control the computer's hardware and provide a platform on which application software runs.
scheme.explanation: System software works for the computer itself; application software works for the user's task.

questions.title: Which is application software?
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of **application** software?

scheme.mark_scheme: C
scheme.explanation: A web browser lets the user do a task (view web pages). A defragmenter (utility), a driver and a compiler (translator) are all system software.

questions.title: System or application?
questions.text: Tick (✓) **one** box in each row to show whether the software is **system** software or **application** software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Antivirus → System; Spreadsheet → Application; Linux → System; Photo-editing → Application; Graphics card driver → System; Online banking app → Application

Six correct (3); four or five (2); two or three (1)
scheme.ai_instructions: Award 3 for six correct rows, 2 for four or five, 1 for two or three. A row with two ticks is wrong.
scheme.explanation: Programs that maintain or run the computer (antivirus, OS, driver) are system software; programs for a user's task are applications.

questions.title: Applications and the OS
questions.text: Application software can run on a computer that has no operating system.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: Applications run on top of the operating system and use its services (memory, files, devices).

questions.title: Compare system and application software
questions.text: Give **two** differences between system software and application software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each), both sides must be stated or clearly implied:
- System software manages / controls the computer; application software performs a user's task
- System software is needed for the computer to work (OS); application software is not
- System software runs in the background / starts with the computer; applications run when the user opens them
- Users interact directly with applications; little direct interaction with system software
- Applications depend on / run on top of the system software
scheme.model_answer: 1 System software controls the computer, while application software lets the user carry out a task. 2 The computer cannot work without system software (the OS), but it can work without applications.
scheme.ai_instructions: Each box must state a difference, not only an example. Do not award the same idea twice.

questions.title: Purpose of the operating system
questions.text: Describe the purpose of an **operating system**.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each):
- Manages the hardware / resources (memory, processor, devices, files)
- Provides a user interface
- Provides a platform for applications to run / allows applications to use the hardware
- Provides security / user accounts / access rights
- Hides the complexity of the hardware from the user
scheme.model_answer: It manages the computer's resources such as memory, processor time and devices, and provides a user interface and a platform on which applications can run.

questions.title: Match system software to purpose
questions.text: Match each type of system software to its purpose.

right.text: Maintains, protects or optimises the computer
Pre-written, tested code that other programs can call
Converts source code into machine code
Lets the OS communicate with a particular hardware device

scheme.mark_scheme: Utility–R1, Library–R2, Translator–R3, Driver–R4. One mark per correct match.

questions.title: Select the utilities
questions.text: Select **two** programs that are **utility** programs.

scheme.mark_scheme: A and C. One mark each; a mark is lost for each incorrect option selected.
scheme.explanation: Compression and backup maintain the computer's data. Presentation software is an application; an interpreter is a translator.

questions.title: Purpose of a utility
questions.text: Describe the purpose of a **utility program** and give **one** example.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Purpose: maintains / analyses / optimises / protects the computer system; helps the computer run efficiently or safely (1)
- Example: antivirus, firewall, defragmenter, backup, compression, disk clean-up, encryption, disk formatter, disk checker (1)
scheme.model_answer: A utility maintains and optimises the computer so it runs efficiently and safely, for example a disk defragmenter.

questions.title: How defragmentation helps
questions.text: Explain how a **disk defragmenter** improves the performance of a computer with a magnetic hard disk.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- It moves the fragments / parts of each file so they are stored together in continuous blocks / groups free space together (1)
- so the read/write head moves less / files can be read (and written) faster (1)

points.criterion: Rearranges file fragments into continuous blocks
Less head movement / faster access to files

scheme.model_answer: It rearranges the scattered fragments of each file so they are stored next to each other, so the read/write head moves less and files are opened faster.

questions.title: Defragmenting an SSD
questions.text: Defragmenting a solid-state drive (SSD) makes files open much faster.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: An SSD has no moving read/write head, so the position of file fragments hardly affects speed; defragmenting only adds wear.

questions.title: Which utility?
questions.text: Complete the table by writing the name of the **utility program** that would solve each problem.

prefill: A file is too large to send as an e-mail attachment
A laptop's data must be recoverable if the laptop is stolen
Files on a hard disk open slowly because they are split into many parts
A downloaded file may contain a virus

scheme.mark_scheme:
1 Compression (1)
2 Backup (accept encryption only if recovery is not the point — here backup) (1)
3 Disk defragmenter (1)
4 Antivirus (1)
scheme.explanation: Compression reduces file size; backup copies data so it can be restored; defragmentation joins file fragments; antivirus detects and removes malware.

questions.title: Why a device driver is needed
questions.text: A school buys a new 3D printer. Explain why a **device driver** must be installed before the printer can be used.

scheme.mark_scheme:

- It translates the OS's general commands into instructions that this specific device / model understands (1)
- (Without it the OS does not know how to use the device) (1)
[Max 2]

points.criterion: Allows the OS to communicate with the device
Translates commands into instructions specific to that device

scheme.model_answer: The driver allows the operating system to communicate with the printer, by translating the OS's general print commands into instructions that this particular printer model understands.

questions.title: What a library is
questions.text:
Complete the sentences.

A program library is a collection of pre-written and pre-[[1]] code. A programmer can [[2]] a library function from their own program instead of writing the code again. A library that is joined to the program only when the program runs is called a [[3]] library.

scheme.mark_scheme: (1) tested / compiled (2) call / use / import (3) dynamic / shared
scheme.explanation: Libraries contain pre-written, pre-tested code; dynamic (shared) libraries such as DLL files are linked at run time.

questions.title: Advantages of libraries
questions.text: State **two** advantages to a programmer of using library routines.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Any two (1 each):
- Saves time / the code does not have to be written again
- Code is already tested so it is reliable / has fewer errors
- Can use complex functions without expert knowledge
- Shared by many programs / saves storage or memory
- Updates to the library improve all programs that use it
scheme.model_answer: 1 It saves development time because the code is already written. 2 The code has already been tested, so it is more reliable.
scheme.ai_instructions: 'Saves time' and 'faster to develop' are the same point.

questions.title: Library or utility
questions.text: A program library is a program that the user opens to keep the computer running efficiently.

scheme.mark_scheme: False.
scheme.explanation: That describes a utility. A library is code that other programs call; the user does not run it directly.

into machine code the CPU can execute

scheme.model_answer: A translator converts source code written in a high-level or assembly language into machine code that the processor can execute.

questions.title: Types of application software

questions.title: Define bespoke software
questions.text: Define the term **bespoke software**.

scheme.mark_scheme: Software written / developed specially for one organisation / user to meet its specific requirements (1)

points.criterion: Written for a specific client to meet its exact requirements

scheme.model_answer: Software that is written specially for one organisation to meet its exact requirements.

questions.title: Bespoke: advantage and disadvantage
questions.text: State **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of implementing bespoke software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Advantage (1): meets the exact / specific requirements; no unnecessary features; the organisation owns / controls the code and can change it; gives an advantage over competitors; can be made compatible with existing systems

Disadvantage (1): higher cost; takes a long time to develop; may contain more bugs (fewer users have tested it); support only from the developer / no user community
scheme.model_answer: Advantage: it is built to meet the organisation's exact requirements. Disadvantage: it is expensive and takes a long time to develop.

questions.title: Why buy general-purpose software
questions.text: A small shop wants to keep records of its daily sales. Give **one** reason why the shop should buy **general-purpose** software instead of ordering bespoke software.

scheme.mark_scheme: Any one (1): available immediately; cheaper because it is mass-produced / development costs shared; well tested by many users so fewer bugs; large user community / tutorials / support available; the shop's needs are simple / common

questions.title: Special-purpose vs bespoke
questions.text: Explain the difference between **special-purpose** software and **bespoke** software.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Special-purpose software does one specific task but is sold off the shelf to many users (1)
- Bespoke software is written for one particular organisation / client to its own requirements (1)

points.criterion: Special-purpose: one task, sold to many users
Bespoke: made for one client's requirements

scheme.model_answer: Special-purpose software performs one particular task but is sold to many different users, whereas bespoke software is written for one organisation to meet its own requirements.
scheme.ai_instructions: Both sides are needed for 2 marks. 'Special-purpose does one task' alone is 1 mark.

questions.title: Software for a clinic
questions.text:
A private clinic with one doctor wants software to book patient appointments. It has a small budget and needs the system next week. A developer offers to write a **bespoke** system in four months.

Discuss whether the clinic should buy **off-the-shelf** appointment software or order the **bespoke** system. Justify your answer.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Up to 4 marks.
- Off-the-shelf is cheaper — suits the small budget (1)
- Off-the-shelf is available immediately — needed next week; bespoke takes four months (1)
- Off-the-shelf is well tested / has support and tutorials (1)
- Bespoke would match the clinic's exact requirements / unique features (1), but the clinic's needs are common / simple (1)
- Conclusion: off-the-shelf (special-purpose) software, justified by the scenario (1)

points.criterion: Cost point linked to the small budget
Time point linked to 'next week' vs four months
Valid point about bespoke (benefit or drawback)

scheme.model_answer: Off-the-shelf software is cheaper because many clinics share its cost, which suits the small budget, and it can be installed immediately, while the bespoke system would take four months. Bespoke software would fit the clinic's exact needs, but booking appointments is a common task, so ready-made software will do it. The clinic should buy off-the-shelf software.
scheme.ai_instructions: Points must be linked to the scenario for full marks. A conclusion for bespoke can get at most 2 marks.

questions.title: Choosing software for a school
questions.text:
A school needs software to record pupils' marks and produce reports. It is considering three options:

1. a **general-purpose** spreadsheet package,
2. a **special-purpose** gradebook program,
3. a **bespoke** system written by a software company.

Evaluate the three options and recommend one for the school.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Spreadsheet (max 2): cheap / may already be owned; flexible; but teachers must build tables and formulas themselves / more errors / not designed for reports

Gradebook (max 2): designed for this task / ready-made reports; available immediately; cheaper than bespoke; but may not follow the school's own grading rules / unneeded features

Bespoke (max 2): exactly fits the school's rules / links with the timetable; but expensive and slow to develop; fewer users so bugs may remain

Recommendation (1–2): a justified choice linked to budget / time / how unusual the requirements are

points.criterion: Second valid point for any option

scheme.model_answer: A spreadsheet is cheap and the school probably already has it, but teachers would have to create their own formulas and report layouts, which takes time and can cause errors. A special-purpose gradebook is designed for recording marks and producing reports, is available immediately and is tested by many schools, but it may not follow the school's own grading rules. A bespoke system would match the school's rules exactly and could link to its timetable, but it is expensive and would take months to develop. I recommend the gradebook, because recording marks is a common task, so the school gets the needed features quickly at a much lower cost than bespoke software.
scheme.ai_instructions: Any justified recommendation can get full marks. Do not award marks for describing the categories without evaluating them.

summary: How software is classified into system software and application software, what the operating system, utilities, drivers, libraries and translators are for, and how general-purpose, special-purpose and bespoke applications differ.

theory.title: What software is and how it is classified

blocks.content: **Hardware** is the physical equipment of a computer. **Software** is the set of **programs** (instructions) and the **data** they use that tell the hardware what to do. Without software, hardware cannot do anything useful.
A collection of programs, data and documentation that instructs a computer how to carry out tasks.
Every program belongs to one of **two main classes**. The class depends on **who the program works for**: the computer itself, or the user's real-world task.

Programs that **manage, control and maintain the computer** and provide a **platform** on which other software runs. The user rarely works with it directly. Examples: operating system, utility programs, device drivers, libraries, translators.

Programs that let the user **carry out a real-world task** — writing a report, editing a photo, paying for goods, booking a ticket. Applications run **on top of the operating system** and cannot run without it.

blocks.title: Classify each program
blocks.content:
| Program | Class | Subcategory |
|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 | System | Operating system |
| Antivirus scanner | System | Utility |
| Printer driver | System | Device driver |
| Python interpreter | System | Translator |
| The `math` module used by a Python program | System | Library |
| Microsoft Excel | Application | General-purpose |
| A payroll program | Application | Special-purpose |
| A booking system written only for one airline | Application | Bespoke |

1. Ask: does it help **the computer** (system) or **the user's task** (application)?
2. Then name the **subcategory**: OS, utility, driver, library, translator — or general-purpose, special-purpose, bespoke.
3. If the question says "explain", add **why**: *"An antivirus is system software because it maintains the computer rather than doing a user's task."*

blocks.title: Firmware
blocks.content: **Firmware** is system software stored permanently in **ROM / flash memory** on a device (e.g. the BIOS/UEFI that starts a PC, or the program inside a washing machine). It starts the hardware and loads the operating system.

System software that **manages the computer's hardware and software resources**, provides a **user interface** and a **platform** on which applications run. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS.
The purpose of the OS is to **hide the complexity of the hardware** from the user and from applications, and to **share resources** (processor, memory, devices) fairly and safely.

items.title: Memory management
items.content: Allocates main memory to programs and data, keeps programs from using each other's memory, frees memory when a program closes, uses virtual memory when RAM is full.

items.title: Processor management
items.content: Schedules which process uses the CPU and for how long, so that several programs appear to run at the same time (**multitasking**).

items.title: File management
items.content: Creates, names, saves, copies, moves and deletes files; organises folders; controls access to files.

items.title: Input/output and peripheral management
items.content: Communicates with devices through **drivers**; handles interrupts and buffers data for printers, keyboards, disks.

items.title: Security and user accounts
items.content: Log-in with user names and passwords, **access rights** to files and folders, firewall, updates.

items.title: User interface
items.content: Lets the user communicate with the computer — graphical (GUI), command-line, menu-driven, touch or voice.

items.title: Error handling
items.content: Detects and reports errors (e.g. a device not responding) and recovers where possible.

blocks.title: Learn more
blocks.content: The functions and types of operating systems are covered in detail in the topics **Operating systems** (Grade 11) and **OS types** (Grade 12). For this topic you need to be able to describe the **purpose** of the OS.
A small system program that **maintains, analyses, optimises or protects** the computer. Utilities do not do a user's real-world task; they help the computer work well.

blocks.title: Common utility programs
rows: Scans files, e-mails and memory; compares them with known virus signatures and suspicious behaviour; quarantines or deletes infected files
Protects data and the system from malware
Checks incoming and outgoing network traffic against rules and blocks unauthorised connections
Moves the scattered fragments of files on a **magnetic hard disk** together into continuous blocks
Files are read faster; the read/write head moves less
Copies files to another medium or the cloud, often on a schedule; can restore them
Data can be recovered after loss, damage or ransomware
Saves storage space and transmission time
Finds and removes temporary, duplicate and unneeded files
Scrambles data with a key so only authorised users can read it
Prepares a disk for use by creating a file system
A new disk can store files
Scans a disk for bad sectors and file-system errors and repairs them
Shows CPU, memory and network use of each process
Helps find slow or faulty programs

blocks.content:
Before:  | A1 | B1 | A2 | -- | B2 | A3 |     file A is in 3 places, file B in 2
After:   | A1 | A2 | A3 | B1 | B2 | -- |     each file is continuous; free space together
blocks.caption: Defragmentation puts the parts of each file next to each other

blocks.content: Defragmentation helps **magnetic hard disks** because their head must move to each fragment. **Solid-state drives (SSDs)** have no moving parts, so defragmenting them gives no speed benefit and causes unnecessary wear.

A small system program that lets the **operating system communicate with a particular hardware device** (printer, graphics card, scanner). It translates the OS's general commands into the specific instructions that device understands.

items: Each model of device can work differently, so it needs its **own driver**.
Without the correct driver, the OS cannot use the device, or can use only basic functions.
Drivers are often installed automatically (*plug and play*) and are updated to fix errors or add features.

blocks.title: A driver in action
blocks.content: The user presses **Print** in a word processor → the application asks the **OS** to print → the OS passes the document to the **printer driver** → the driver converts it into commands for that specific printer model → the printer prints.
A collection of **pre-written, pre-compiled and pre-tested code** — functions, procedures, classes — that programmers can **call from their own programs** instead of writing that code again.

import math        # standard maths library
import random      # random-number library

radius = 4
area = math.pi * radius ** 2          # constant from the library
side = math.sqrt(49)                  # library function
dice = random.randint(1, 6)           # library function
print(round(area, 2), side, dice)
blocks.caption: A program that uses library functions instead of writing them from scratch

items.title: Advantages of using libraries
items.content:
- **Saves development time** — the code is already written.
- Code is **already tested**, so it is more **reliable** and has fewer errors.
- Programmers can use **complex functions** (graphics, encryption, maths, networking) without expert knowledge.
- One library can be **shared by many programs**, saving storage and memory (e.g. Windows **DLL** files).
- When the library is updated, all programs that use it can benefit.

items.title: Disadvantages
items.content:
- The programmer depends on someone else's code — errors or security flaws in the library affect the program.
- A library may contain **many functions that are not needed**, making the program larger.
- A program may stop working if the library version it needs is missing or changed.

blocks.title: Static and dynamic libraries
rows: When it is joined to the program
Larger — library code is copied in
Needs the library on the user's computer?
Replacing the library updates all programs

blocks.content: A **library** is not a program the user runs. It is code that **other programs** call. A **utility** is a complete program that the user (or the OS) runs to maintain the computer.
The processor can only execute **machine code** (binary instructions). Programs written in **high-level languages** (Python, C#, Java) or **assembly language** must be translated first.
System software that **converts program code** written in a programming language (**source code**) into **machine code** (**object code**) that the processor can execute.

blocks.title: The three translators
rows: **One statement at a time**, executing it immediately
Stops at the **first error** it meets
Runs the executable — no translation needed
Must be translated **every time** it runs

items.title: Advantages of a compiler
items.content:
- The compiled program **runs faster** — translation is done once.
- Only the **executable** is given to users, so the **source code stays secret**.
- The user does not need the compiler to run the program.

items.title: Advantages of an interpreter
items.content:
- **Easier debugging** — the program stops at the line with the error.
- Changes can be tested **immediately** without re-compiling.
- The same source code can run on different platforms that have the interpreter.

blocks.title: Learn more
blocks.content: Compilation stages (lexical analysis, syntax analysis, code generation, optimisation) are studied in **Program compilation stages** (Grade 12), and language generations in **Translators and language generations**.
Application software is divided into three subcategories according to **how many tasks** it does and **for whom it was made**.

items.title: General-purpose software
items.content: Can be used for **many different tasks** by many different users. Bought **off the shelf** (ready-made) or downloaded. *Examples: word processor, spreadsheet, presentation software, database package, web browser, e-mail client.*

items.title: Special-purpose software
items.content: Designed to carry out **one specific task or type of task**, but sold to **many users**. Also off the shelf. *Examples: payroll software, accounting software, tax calculator, route planner, photo-editing software, school timetable program, a game.*

items.title: Bespoke (custom-written) software
items.content: **Written specially for one organisation** to meet its **exact requirements**, by its own programmers or a hired company. *Examples: the booking system of a particular airline, the control program of one factory's machines, a bank's own online-banking system.*

blocks.title: The same task — three kinds of software
blocks.content:
A school needs to record pupils' marks:
- **General-purpose:** the teachers use a **spreadsheet** (e.g. Excel) and create their own tables and formulas.
- **Special-purpose:** the school buys a **gradebook program** designed only for recording and reporting marks.
- **Bespoke:** the school hires developers to write a **marks system** that follows the school's own grading rules and links to its timetable.

blocks.title: Off-the-shelf (general / special purpose) vs bespoke
rows: Cheaper — development cost is shared by many buyers
Expensive — one client pays for all development
Takes a **long time** to analyse, design, write and test
May contain unneeded features or lack some needed ones; the company may have to change how it works
Used and tested by many people, so most bugs are already found
Fewer users, so bugs may remain
Large user community, tutorials, forums, training courses
Regular updates from the vendor, but the company cannot choose the changes
Can be changed whenever the company wants (it may own the code)
Competitors can buy the same product
May not fit the company's existing systems
Built to work with existing systems

blocks.title: Choosing for a scenario
items: If the task is **common** (letters, spreadsheets, e-mail) → **general-purpose**.
If the task is **specific but common to many organisations** (payroll, accounting) → **special-purpose**.
If the organisation has **unique requirements**, needs to integrate with its own systems, or wants an advantage over competitors, **and** has enough **money and time** → **bespoke**.
Always justify with the **scenario**: budget, deadline, how unusual the requirements are.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Describe the purpose of a utility program. Give one example. [2]**
A utility program **maintains, analyses or optimises the computer** / helps the computer run efficiently and safely (1), for example an **antivirus** that detects and removes malware (1).

**Q: Explain why a programmer would use a library. [2]**
The functions are **already written and tested** (1), **so** development is **faster** / the program is **more reliable** (1).

**Q: State one advantage and one disadvantage of implementing bespoke software. [2]**
Advantage: it is **custom-built to meet the exact requirements** of the organisation (1). Disadvantage: it has a **higher cost** / **takes a long time** to develop (1).

**Q: A store wants to computerise its daily sales records. Give one reason the store should buy general-purpose software. [1]**
It is **available immediately** / it is **cheaper** because it is mass-produced / it is well tested by many users / there is a large user community for help (any one).

- Calling a web browser or a game **system software** — they do a user's task, so they are **application software**.
- Confusing **special-purpose** (one task, many buyers) with **bespoke** (made for **one** organisation).
- Writing "bespoke software is better" without **comparing** — say *what* is better (fits the requirements exactly) and the cost (expensive, slow to develop).
- Saying a compiler "runs the program" — it **translates** it; the executable is run later.
- Describing a utility as "a useful program" — say **what it does for the computer**.

blocks.title: Check yourself
items: What is the difference between system software and application software? Give two examples of each.
Name five types of system software and describe the purpose of each.
Name four utility programs and what each does.
Give two advantages of using libraries.
Compare a compiler and an interpreter in two ways.
Define general-purpose, special-purpose and bespoke software, with an example of each.
Give two advantages and two disadvantages of bespoke software compared with off-the-shelf software.
